command: PYTHONPATH=/tmp/whl_extract MISTRALRS_GRAMMAR_FAST_FORWARD=1 python3 ff_harness.py run --mode equality --flag on --model-id Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --arch Qwen2 --max-tokens 4 --seed 1 --schema-file plans/ff-round-two/fixtures/partial.schema.json --plan attempt1 --label smoke
traceback_tail: ValueError: cannot seed the CPU rng with set_seed

diagnosis.reproduced_minimally: mistralrs.Runner(which=Which.Plain(model_id='Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct', arch=Architecture.Qwen2), seed=42) raises the same ValueError immediately, before any network request (no partial download appeared under ~/.cache/huggingface).
diagnosis.root_cause_located: candle-core's CPU RNG device in this build has no settable seed: the wheel's compiled strings include the literal pair 'cannot get the CPU rng seed with get_current_seed' / 'cannot seed the CPU rng with set_seed', both unconditional (not model- or dtype-gated).
diagnosis.confirms_device_specific_not_ff_specific: Runner(which=..., seed=None) (bypassing ff_harness.py, diagnostic only) proceeds past construction and starts downloading the model -- confirmed by an INFO log line ('Could not load token at ... using no HF token') and network activity, cut off only by a 15s diagnostic timeout. So the blocker is specifically 'a concrete seed value passed to Runner on a CPU device', not the model id, tokenizer, or grammar.
diagnosis.why_the_harness_cannot_avoid_it: ff_harness.py's argparse defines --seed with default=42 (never None) and build_plain_runner() passes runner_kwargs = dict(which=which, seed=args.seed) unconditionally -- there is no CLI flag to omit seed. Per this task's constraints, ff_harness.py was not modified to route around this.

conclusion: This is a container/build capability gap (CPU-only wheel + a harness interface that always seeds + no CUDA/Metal device available to construct a Runner that supports set_seed), not a finding about grammar fast-forward. No inference was reached, so this run says nothing about mistralrs_grammar_ff_splices_staged_total.
